# Board Game Designer Skill for Muse

Takes a board game idea from "wouldn't it be cool if" to a playtestable prototype: a design one-pager (hook, core loop, tension source), a prototype spec buildable from household stationery tonight, first-pass balance numbers explicitly flagged as guesses to tune, and a 3-session playtest protocol with honest kill criteria. It forces the designer's questions in the order working designers ask them — loop before theme, tension before content, cardboard before art. Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: this is a design-thinking framework, not an art or manufacturing tool — it deliberately forbids art until a prototype survives five plays, and it never promises market outcomes. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
